title: The Rain Garden Beneath the Pavement

source_links.title: US EPA: Environmental Benefits of Green Infrastructure

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: After an afternoon storm, students notice that rainwater covers a paved crossing near their school.
sentences.ja: 午後の嵐の後、生徒たちは学校近くの舗装された横断歩道に雨水がたまっているのに気づきます。

sentences.en: The road appears dry the following morning, yet the students wonder where all that water went.
sentences.ja: 翌朝道路は乾いて見えますが、生徒たちはその水がどこへ行ったか疑問に思います。

sentences.en: In many developed areas, rain flows across hard surfaces and enters drainage pipes rather than soaking into the ground.
sentences.ja: 多くの開発地域では雨は地面に染み込まず、硬い表面を流れて排水管に入ります。

sentences.en: When heavy rain arrives faster than the pipes can carry it away, streets may flood.
sentences.ja: 排水管の処理能力より速く大雨が降ると、道路が浸水することがあります。

sentences.en: The United States Environmental Protection Agency describes green infrastructure as methods that capture or absorb stormwater.
sentences.ja: 米国環境保護庁は雨水を捕らえたり吸収したりする方法をグリーンインフラとして説明しています。

sentences.en: These approaches do not eliminate all flooding, but they can reduce runoff where local conditions allow.
sentences.ja: こうした方法はすべての洪水をなくしませんが、地域条件が許せば雨水の表面流出を減らせます。

sentences.en: One example is a rain garden, a shallow area planted with vegetation suited to its environment.
sentences.ja: 一例は環境に適した植物を植えた浅いくぼ地である雨庭です。

sentences.en: Instead of sending every drop directly into a pipe, a rain garden temporarily holds some stormwater.
sentences.ja: すべての雨滴を直接排水管へ送る代わりに、雨庭は一部の雨水を一時的に保持します。

sentences.en: For example, runoff from a nearby roof can be guided toward a carefully designed planted area.
sentences.ja: 例えば近くの屋根からの流出水を、慎重に設計した植栽区域へ導けます。

sentences.en: Soil and plants can help water enter the ground, while some pollutants may be filtered along the way.
sentences.ja: 土と植物は水が地中へ入る助けとなり、途中で一部の汚染物質もろ過される場合があります。

sentences.en: However, a garden that has not been properly designed could collect water in the wrong place.
sentences.ja: しかし適切に設計されていない庭では、望ましくない場所に水が集まるかもしれません。

sentences.en: The amount of rain, the shape of the land, and the characteristics of the soil all matter.
sentences.ja: 雨量、土地の形、土の特徴がすべて重要です。

sentences.en: The school proposes replacing a small section of unused pavement with a rain garden.
sentences.ja: 学校は使われていない舗装の一部を雨庭に変えることを提案します。

sentences.en: Before planting anything, the team consults people who understand drainage and local safety requirements.
sentences.ja: 何かを植える前に、チームは排水と地域の安全条件を理解する人々に相談します。

sentences.en: In addition, they consider whether the proposed garden might block a wheelchair route or a school entrance.
sentences.ja: さらに予定地が車いすの通路や学校の入口をふさがないか考えます。

sentences.en: The cheapest location is not necessarily the best location if it creates difficulties for other users.
sentences.ja: 他の利用者に困難を生むなら、最も安い場所が最善とは限りません。

sentences.en: Long-term maintenance is also necessary because plants may die and sediment may accumulate.
sentences.ja: 植物が枯れたり土砂がたまったりするため、長期的な維持管理も必要です。

sentences.en: A responsible project involves planning for its future rather than celebrating only the day it opens.
sentences.ja: 責任ある活動は開設の日だけを祝うのでなく、その後を計画することを含みます。

sentences.en: Students can help evaluate the project without pretending that a single observation proves success.
sentences.ja: 生徒は一度の観察だけで成功を証明したと思い込まずに活動を評価できます。

sentences.en: They might compare photographs of the same area after similar rain events at different times.
sentences.ja: 似た雨の後の同じ場所の写真を異なる時点で比べられます。

sentences.en: They should also record circumstances such as rainfall intensity and whether nearby drains were blocked.
sentences.ja: 雨の強さや近くの排水口が詰まっていたかなどの状況も記録すべきです。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, a useful conclusion must acknowledge that weather conditions can vary considerably.
sentences.ja: それでも天候条件には大きな違いがあることを結論で認める必要があります。

sentences.en: The real question is not whether a garden looks attractive but whether it makes the surrounding area more resilient.
sentences.ja: 本当の問いは庭が美しいかではなく、周辺地域をより災害に強くするかです。

sentences.en: Understanding that distinction turns a decorative space into an opportunity for scientific inquiry.
sentences.ja: その違いを理解すると装飾的な空間が科学的探究の機会になります。

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the passage's main message?
options: Plants can replace every drainage pipe.
Rain gardens can help manage runoff, but design and evaluation matter.
Rain never enters the ground in cities.
School grounds should contain no pavement.
questions.explanation_ja: 雨庭の利点と設計・検証の条件が主題です。

questions.prompt: Why can streets flood during heavy rain?
options: Drainage pipes may not carry away water quickly enough.
Every sidewalk is made of soil.
questions.explanation_ja: 排水管の能力を超える雨が原因になり得ます。

questions.prompt: Why is runoff from a roof directed toward a rain garden?
options: Some water can be stored and absorbed rather than immediately entering pipes.
A garden needs no drainage plan.
Rain gardens are designed only for decoration.
questions.explanation_ja: 流出水の一部を一時保持し浸透させるためです。

questions.prompt: Which conditions matter when designing a rain garden?
options: Only the color of the flowers.
Only the distance to a library.
Rainfall, land shape, and soil characteristics.
questions.explanation_ja: 降雨量、地形、土の性質を挙げています。

questions.prompt: Whom does the school consult before planting?
options: People familiar with drainage and safety requirements.
questions.explanation_ja: 排水と安全に詳しい人へ相談します。

questions.prompt: Why might the cheapest site be unsuitable?
options: Plants always grow better on expensive land.
Every project must be near a road.
It might obstruct access for people using wheelchairs.
The area may have too many signs.
questions.explanation_ja: 移動のしやすさを損ねる可能性があるためです。

options: Better able to cope with difficulties.
questions.explanation_ja: resilientは困難に対応し回復できる状態です。

questions.prompt: What should students record when evaluating the garden?
options: Only the color of nearby shoes.
Rainfall conditions and possible blocked drains.
questions.explanation_ja: 雨の状況や排水口の詰まりなどを記録します。

questions.prompt: Why is a single observation insufficient?
options: Weather conditions can vary between observations.
questions.explanation_ja: 条件の違いが結果に影響し得るためです。

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence suggest?
options: A garden is valuable only if it is beautiful.
Every school must build the same project.
An ordinary space can become a place for evidence-based investigation.
questions.explanation_ja: 身近な庭を科学的な探究活動につなげる結論です。
